business: NOCTIS, a smart bedside companion by offhours (EUR 120)
target: Design-aware adults in Europe, 25 to 45, with disposable income, who scroll in bed and use their phone as alarm, and care about sleep and how their home looks

behaviours.name: Design buyer
behaviours.how: Pays more for objects that look good in the home; follows design brands and studios.

behaviours.name: Phone-in-bed scroller
behaviours.how: Knows they scroll too long at night and has tried screen-time limits without success.

behaviours.name: Gadget sceptic
behaviours.how: Feels most smart devices are overpriced and do things the phone already does.

behaviours.name: Deal hunter
behaviours.how: Waits for discounts and compares prices across Amazon and brands.

behaviours.name: Sleep-curious
behaviours.how: Reads about sleep, owns a watch or ring, wary of health claims.

behaviours.name: Smart-home owner
behaviours.how: Already has a smart speaker or display and an ecosystem.

objections: EUR 120 is a lot when my phone already does this for free
I already own an Echo or Nest that does alarm and weather
Will the alarm still work if the Wi-Fi is down
It is a new brand from a student company, will it exist next year
I need my phone near me anyway, for emergencies or the kids
Does it listen to me all night, what about privacy
How accurate can a sleep and snoring estimate from a microphone be
habits: you check your phone for about 30 minutes before falling asleep
your phone charges on the bedside table and is the first thing you look at in the morning
you use your phone alarm and snooze it more than once
you have thought about leaving the phone in another room but never did
